historical_references.reference: Mirzaq was a renowned Persian poet and scholar of the Safavid Empire in the 16th century. He is most famous for his work 'Masnavi-e-Miraq', a Persian epic poem written in the genre of 'mathnavi' which consists of rhymed couplets. This work is considered a major contribution to Persian literature.
historical_references.context: The Safavid Empire was a major power in the Middle East from the 16th to 18th centuries. Persian literature flourished during this period, and Mirzaq's work is an important part of it.

historical_references.reference: Mirzaq Ghaffari was a famous Persian calligrapher and painter during the late Timurid and early Mughal periods in the late 15th and early 16th centuries. He is known for his mastery of the 'thuluth' script and created many beautiful works on paper and manuscripts. His work was influential in the development of Mughal art.
historical_references.context: The Timurid Empire was a major power in Central Asia from the late 14th to the early 16th centuries. Mirzaq Ghaffari worked during the transition between the Timurid and Mughal periods, and his work reflects the cultural exchange between these two empires.
